title: Storage Systems: Allocation, Lifecycle, Retention, and Backup
bodyMarkdown:
## Provisioning and Governing Storage

Architects must match each workload to the right storage product, control cost through lifecycle policies, enforce compliance retention, plan for growth, and guarantee recoverability.

### Choosing a storage product

| Product | Type | Best for |
|---------|------|----------|
| Cloud Storage | Object | Unstructured data, backups, data lakes, static assets |
| Persistent Disk / Hyperdisk | Block | VM boot/data disks; Hyperdisk tunes IOPS/throughput independently |
| Filestore | File (NFS) | Shared POSIX file systems, lift-and-shift apps |
| Cloud SQL / AlloyDB | Relational | OLTP databases |
| Spanner | Relational, global | Horizontally scalable, strongly consistent global OLTP |
| Bigtable | NoSQL wide-column | High-throughput time-series/IoT |
| Firestore | NoSQL document | App/mobile backends |

### Cloud Storage classes and lifecycle

Storage classes trade storage price for retrieval cost and minimum storage duration:

- **Standard** — hot, no minimum duration.
- **Nearline** — ~30-day minimum, infrequent access.
- **Coldline** — ~90-day minimum, quarterly access.
- **Archive** — ~365-day minimum, rare access, lowest storage price.

**Object Lifecycle Management** transitions or deletes objects by age, version, or matching conditions (e.g., Standard -> Nearline at 30 days -> Coldline at 365 days, delete at 7 years). **Autoclass** automatically moves objects between classes based on access patterns when those patterns are unpredictable.

### Retention and immutability (WORM)

- **Retention policy** sets a minimum period during which objects cannot be deleted or overwritten.
- **Bucket Lock (retention policy lock)** makes the policy permanent — it can be increased but never decreased or removed, even by owners. This satisfies WORM/regulatory holds.
- **Object holds** (event-based, temporary) apply per-object legal holds.
- **Object Versioning** and **soft delete** protect against accidental overwrite/delete (operational protection, not regulatory immutability).

### Data transfer and latency

- **gcloud storage / parallel composite uploads** — online, link-bound.
- **Storage Transfer Service** — managed online transfers (cloud-to-cloud, on-prem agents, scheduled).
- **Transfer Appliance** — offline, rugged physical device for large datasets (tens of TB to PB) where the WAN link is too slow.
- Choose by *data size vs. link speed vs. deadline*: large volumes on modest links -> Transfer Appliance.

### Backup, recovery, and growth

- **Backup and DR Service** — centralized, policy-driven, application-consistent backups with retention and isolated **backup vaults**; fast restore for RPO/RTO targets.
- **Persistent Disk snapshots** — incremental, can be scheduled via resource policies.
- **Cloud SQL automated backups + point-in-time recovery** for database RPO.
- Plan **growth** with autoscaling storage, quotas, and lifecycle tiering to keep cost predictable.

### Best practices

- Encrypt with CMEK where compliance requires key control.
- Match storage class to the access pattern; let lifecycle/Autoclass automate transitions.
- Lock retention for compliance; test restores against RTO regularly.
